books.section: Topic 5.8 Military Conflict in the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: The Pending Contest (Oliver Evans Woods, Philadelphia, 1864)

stimulus.source_note: The Pending Contest, published by Oliver Evans Woods, Philadelphia, 1864 (Library of Congress, LCCN2008661659). Public domain. Image from the shared pool.
stimulus.text: The cartoon, titled “The Pending Contest,” shows two men fighting with clubs. One wears a sash reading “SECESSION”; the other wears a sash reading “The PEOPLE shall Rule!” and holds a rope. Behind them, the Emperor Napoleon of France and John Bull of England watch. Below the image, the Citizen Soldier says his country's flag was “trampled under foot” and his countrymen's ships destroyed, yet he keeps fighting. At the bottom it reads: “Although all Copperheads call themselves Democrats, nevertheless, all Democrats are not Copperheads.”

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The caption at the bottom says, “Although all Copperheads call themselves Democrats, nevertheless, all Democrats are not Copperheads.” The cartoonist’s point is that

options.text: all Democrats in the North opposed the war effort.
options.misconception: The caption says the opposite: not all Democrats were Copperheads.

options.text: opposition to the war came from one Democratic faction.

options.misconception: Copperheads called themselves Democrats, and the cartoonist takes that label seriously.
Lincoln led the war effort; the Copperheads were his opponents, not his allies.

rationales.A: The caption says the opposite: not all Democrats were Copperheads.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Copperheads were Northern Democrats who opposed the war; many other Democrats supported it.
rationales.C: Copperheads called themselves Democrats, and the cartoonist takes that label seriously.
rationales.D: Lincoln led the war effort; the Copperheads were his opponents, not his allies.
rationales.general:
1. The caption is a piece of logic: all A are B does not mean all B are A.
2. All Copperheads called themselves Democrats, but the party was bigger than that faction.
3. Background from the books: Copperheads were Northern Democrats who opposed the war; many other Democrats supported it.
4. The cartoonist defends ordinary Democrats against being blamed for the Copperheads’ opposition.
Remember: all A are B never proves all B are A: watch the direction of the claim.
